terms.definitionEn: A sequence of text characters represented as a primitive value.
A delimiter that marks the beginning and end of a string literal.
A backslash-based notation for a character with special meaning in text.
The operation of joining text values into a longer sequence.
The number of UTF-16 code units in a string.
A way to access a character-like code unit using a numeric position.
A zero-based position used to access a character in text.
The property that an existing value cannot be altered in place.
A string form delimited by backticks that supports interpolation.
The insertion of an expression's value into a text template.
The conversion of a value to text during an operation that needs a string.
A 16-bit value used as a basic component of JavaScript string indexing.

questions.question: What kind of value is stored in city?
options: An array of four separate values
questions.explanation: Text between matching quotes is a string literal.
The plus operator concatenates two strings directly.
The word contains four UTF-16 code units.

questions.prompt: Fill the index to access the second character.
questions.explanation: String indexes begin at zero, making the second character index 1.
The escape sequence \n represents a line feed.

questions.question: Why is the apostrophe escaped?
options: To convert the apostrophe to a number
So it does not end the single-quoted string early
questions.explanation: The backslash lets an apostrophe appear inside a single-quoted literal.

questions.prompt: Write welcome(name), returning the text 'Welcome, ' followed by name and an exclamation mark.
questions.explanation: Concatenate fixed text around the supplied name.

questions.prompt: Fill the operator that appends a question mark to the existing string.
questions.explanation: Addition-assignment concatenates the new string and stores it back.

questions.prompt: Write makeSentence(noun, verb), returning 'The noun verb.' with the supplied words.
questions.explanation: Place each supplied word between the fixed pieces of text.
String characters cannot be changed by assigning to an indexed position.
Concatenation joins the text and converts the number to text.

questions.prompt: Complete the index expression to print the final character in a non-empty word.
questions.explanation: The final index is one less than the string length.

questions.prompt: Write endsWithMark(text), returning true if text ends with an exclamation mark.
questions.explanation: endsWith checks whether a string ends with the supplied suffix.

questions.prompt: Fill the escape character so the inner double quote is part of the text.
questions.explanation: A backslash escapes a quote that would otherwise end the literal.

questions.question: What kind of result does the plus operator produce here?
options: The number 72, because the digits are multiplied
The string '72', because one operand is a string
A TypeError because the operand types differ
The number 9, because plus always adds numerically
questions.explanation: When plus has a string operand, the other value is converted to text and concatenated.

questions.prompt: Write charAtOrEmpty(text, index), returning the character at index or an empty string when it is missing.
questions.explanation: An out-of-range bracket access is undefined, so nullish coalescing supplies the fallback.

questions.question: Why is a new string assigned instead of changing text[0]?
options: The first character is always read-only because text uses let
slice changes the original string in place
String values are immutable, so the expression constructs a replacement
The plus operator converts the result to an array
questions.explanation: String operations produce new values; they do not mutate the existing string.
The tab escape is one code unit, so the string has three code units.

questions.prompt: Fill the index so the code prints the second character, counting from one in ordinary speech.
questions.explanation: JavaScript uses zero-based indexes, so the second character is at position 1.

questions.prompt: Write repeatWithDash(left, right), joining the strings with exactly one hyphen.
questions.explanation: Insert the separator between the two supplied strings.
A negative slice index counts backward from the end and returns the final three characters.

questions.question: What does it mean that JavaScript strings are immutable?
keyPoints: Existing string values are not changed in place
A variable can be reassigned to a new string
Indexed assignment does not replace a character
questions.modelAnswer: String values cannot be changed in place, so methods and concatenation produce new strings. A variable holding a string can still be reassigned to a different string value.

questions.question: Why can a visible character count differ from a JavaScript string's length?
keyPoints: Some Unicode characters use multiple code units
Combining marks may render with another character
Code points or grapheme segmentation may be needed
questions.modelAnswer: JavaScript's length property counts UTF-16 code units, not necessarily user-perceived characters. Some symbols use multiple code units, and a displayed grapheme can also combine multiple code points.

questions.question: How does the plus operator behave when one operand is a string?
keyPoints: The operation can concatenate rather than add numerically
The other operand is converted to a string
Operand grouping can affect results in longer expressions
Use explicit conversion for clear numeric addition
questions.modelAnswer: When string concatenation applies, the other operand is converted to a string and the text values are joined. In expressions that mix numbers and strings, evaluation order matters, so explicit numeric conversion can make arithmetic intent clear.
